note: Hand-authored from PROJECTION.md, not generated by an implementation. NODE ENCODING (deixis v0.2.0, mandatory node values): a node is { own, children }, where `own` is a hex string for Some(bytes) and null for None, and `children` is a list of [key-hex, node] pairs in AUTHORED order — deixis identity ignores that order. Every node has an own value AND a child map, so the v0.1.0 leaf/struct sum is gone: P(Atom(b)) = { own: b, children: [] } and P(Tuple(xs)) = { own: null, children: kappa(i) -> P(xs[i]) }. `project` cases pin P(value) = node and, read backwards, R(node) = value (laws 1-3). `unrecognized` cases pin R's refusal: a conforming recognizer rejects each node, never repairs it. Each carries a `kind`, which IS normative — the mandatory-value model admits shapes the old sum could not express, and they do not all fail for the same reason: `key_mismatch` is a malformed positional domain, `value_with_children` is a node carrying a payload beside children, which P never emits. The `reason` prose stays informative only. `value_pairs` pin law 4 in BOTH directions: `equal` states left =O right, and a conforming P must make P(left) =D P(right) exactly when it holds. `d_equal_nodes` pin law 5: the two nodes are =D, so R must reach the same outcome and, on success, equal outputs. Equality is over the WHOLE payload: None differs from every Some, and two Somes compare by exact bytes. SCOPE, so this file's self-description matches its schema: laws 1-6 are pinned by the sections above (law 6 is the empty_atom_is_not_empty_tuple pair, and in this model the two empties differ in `own` alone — both are childless); `paths` pin law 7 (ontos-internal#290): the index path resolves in the value IFF the key path (the kappa of each index) resolves in P(value), and on success the node reached is P(subvalue) - the biconditional AND the same-subvalue clause. So laws 1-7 are ALL pinned by the sections above.

unrecognized.name: shifted
unrecognized.reason: one entry, but its key is kappa(1); a 1-entry domain must be exactly { kappa(0) }

unrecognized.name: gap
unrecognized.reason: two entries with keys kappa(0), kappa(2); a 2-entry domain must be exactly { kappa(0), kappa(1) } — gaps are never filled

unrecognized.name: non_positional_key
unrecognized.reason: the key 61 spells no position; named keys are well-formed deixis, not ontos

unrecognized.name: non_canonical_spelling
unrecognized.reason: ff000001 would decode to 1 under a lax reader, but position 1 is spelled 0001; alternate spellings are rejected, never normalized

unrecognized.name: empty_key
unrecognized.reason: the empty key spells no position

unrecognized.name: extra_after_dense_prefix
unrecognized.reason: a dense positional prefix plus a named straggler; the whole domain must be positional

unrecognized.name: child_unrecognized
unrecognized.reason: the outer domain is dense but its child is shifted; recognition is recursive and fails from the inside out

unrecognized.name: value_with_one_child
unrecognized.reason: a present own value beside a child; P gives a payload only to a CHILDLESS node, so this is outside its image — and the key here is a perfectly good kappa(0), which is why blaming a key would be a false explanation

unrecognized.name: empty_value_with_one_child
unrecognized.reason: Some("") is a present value, not an absent one; the empty byte string is an atom's bytes and still forbids children

unrecognized.name: value_with_dense_children
unrecognized.reason: the child domain is exactly { kappa(0), kappa(1) } and is not the problem; the node is refused on its SHAPE, before any key is consulted

unrecognized.name: value_with_malformed_children
unrecognized.reason: both wrong: a payload beside children AND a named key. The shape is decided first, so a conforming face reports value_with_children — the node is not a tuple, so its domain was never required to be positional

unrecognized.name: nested_value_with_children
unrecognized.reason: the outer node is a well-formed tuple of one; the refusal comes from inside it, so recognition fails from the inside out for a shape reason rather than a key reason

d_distinct_nodes.name: absent_is_not_empty_bytes
d_distinct_nodes.reason: law 6 in the mandatory-value model: None and Some("") are different payloads, so the empty tuple and the empty atom are different nodes. A face that compared only `is some` or coerced None to empty bytes would merge them

d_distinct_nodes.name: some_values_compare_by_exact_bytes
d_distinct_nodes.reason: equality is over the whole payload, so two Somes differ when their bytes differ — including by length alone
